summary: Yutaka Ochihara was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986).

Yutaka Takagi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and was a professor at Rissho University (attested 1980–1984).

Yutaka Yoshida is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Hitotsubashi University, later holding posts at Hitotsubashi University (~1989–2006) and Kyoto University (~2006–2020).
Yutaka Yuda was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1958). He served as a professor at Kanagawa University (~1974–2002).

Yuto Kawamura is a researcher in Indology and linguistics. Kawamura held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2020), Kyoto University as a postdoctoral fellow (2015–2018), and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi was a Sinology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University, and Kyushu University. He held posts at Saitama University (~1972–1978), the University of Tokyo (~1978–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Zarawar Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. Khan completed an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018) and was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Tokyo. Ikuno held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1955), served there as professor (~1976–2000), and later was a researcher at the Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University. He worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture (~1930–1949), served as president of Kyoto University (attested 1956–1966), and taught at Bukkyo University (~1961–1972).
Zesei Machida was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as betto at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Zhao Luo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Sen Wang. Luo held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and as a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).
Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed a PhD in sociology at EHESS (2007). Ji has served as Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed an MA at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (2005) and an MA at Lanzhou University (2009).
Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist College (1947) and under Yin Shun (1952). Zhenhua served as manager at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel. Yao held posts at the University of Hong Kong (2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003).

Zhiru Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. Ng served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).
